why: The criterion holds. I compared each check's PASS and FAIL conditions with the words of its expect line. Check 1 only requires the greeting for the name in upper case. Check 2 compares output without --shout against the base and fails on "any difference", which is what "unchanged" means. Including the no-name case is still within "without --shout". Check 3 requires that docs/index.md mentions --shout and explains its effect. That is a fair reading of "documents"; it doesn't demand exact wording or a usage example, which are listed under Advisory. Check 4 requires the PR to be merged and the published page to list --shout, and says to report it as not verifiable before merge. The stricter items are all under "Advisory (not pass/fail conditions)": passing `npm test`, adding a --shout test, the flag working after the name, and a docs usage example. Running `npm test` first is only noted, not graded.
